thread:
maria: heads-up — nightly kernel harness flagged regressions for candidate cand-17 on Ampere longseq runs (seq=4096+).

aj: ugh, saw the alert. is it latency p95 or tail?

maria: mostly p95 and p99. baseline cand-12 p95=38ms, cand-17 p95=62ms on same infra. p50 is similar.

sasha: any change in batching heuristics or kv-cache path in the candidate?

maria: candidate includes the new tiled attention kernel + an altered kv-cache invalidation path (attempt to reduce memory churn). suspect interaction with continuous-batching and long KV reuse.

perf-lab-bot: nightly-harness | run_id=2026-03-15-03 | arch=ampere | kernel=cand-17 | status=FLAGGED | delta_p95=+63% | sample=1000

tariq: can you paste the microbench output? small snippet is fine.

maria: paste below. this is a trimmed harness run for seq=4096, batch=1..8, kv_reuse=on:

```
# cand-12 (baseline) seq=4096 b=1 p50=35.8ms p95=38.2ms p99=48.9ms
# cand-17 (candidate) seq=4096 b=1 p50=36.1ms p95=62.1ms p99=94.7ms
# cand-17 b=4 p95=120ms (high variance)
# log snippet: warn: kv_cache_flush() took 12.4ms; kv_merge waited 3.1ms
```

devon: that kv_cache_flush call stands out. cand-17 changed layout so flush touches more pages? could cause TLB/fault noise.

aj: also note p99 jump — suggests occasional full-scan/backoff in tiled kernel when sequence boundary crosses block. we saw similar on H100 earlier but different trigger.

sasha: can we repro under perf lab with perf counters? try with `harness/repro --arch ampere --kernel cand-17 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --profile perf_events` and attach flamegraphs.

maria: running now. attaching initial perf top:

```
- 28% tiled_attention_impl::compute_block
- 14% kv_cache::shallow_sync
- 9% tiled_attention_impl::sync_for_next_block
- 6% memcpy (hugepages?)
```

perf-lab-bot: collect attached: s3://redwood-perf/cand-17/2026-03-15/ampere/seq4096.tar.gz

tariq: if memcpy and sync are heavy, batching may amplify. auto-batcher picks batch size based on p50 earlier, but p99 degradation isn't considered in pick. maybe autotune scoring needs tail-aware penalty.

devon: agree. quick mitigation: gate cand-17 for seq>2048 on Ampere and allow for shorter seq. fallback to cand-12 for longseq.

aj: +1. also add a microprobe that toggles kv_cache path (new vs old) to measure flush costs isolated. want a perf CI entry for that.

sasha: I'll add the probe to nightly harness (small matrix: seq=1024,2048,4096; batch=1,4) and flag if p95>baseline*1.4.

maria: created PR: https://git.internal/redwood/harness/pulls/482 — adds kv-toggle probe and tail-aware gating metric. rough description in PR.

perf-lab-bot: PR 482 created by sasha — tests added: kv-toggle; gating: p95_ratio>1.4 -> FAIL.

tariq: action items: 1) gate cand-17 for ampere longseq (devon), 2) add kv-toggle probe (sasha), 3) run perf-events repro and attach flamegraphs (maria), 4) update autotune scoring to include p95 penalty (aj). assign owners?

devon: taking #1, will push config change to candidate gating.

sasha: taking #2, I'll land small test tomorrow.

maria: continuing #3 now, will upload artifacts in an hour. initial flamegraph shows hotspots in `kv_cache::shallow_sync` when tiled kernel triggers sync at block boundaries.

aj: I'll prototype p95-penalty change in the autotuner scoring notebook and post numbers. if candidate improves tail after kv path tweak, we can re-eval.

maria: one more note — load on driver during the flagged runs was spiky (driver queue depth oscillation). possible scheduling interaction. adding driver traces to artifact.

devon: good catch. could be that tiled kernel causes many smaller GPU kernels instead of fused ops for longseq in this candidate, increasing overhead.

sasha: okay landing the kv-toggle probe now. will set it to run in the nightly matrix for next 3 nights.

maria: thanks all. will follow up with repro artifacts and a short summary once flamegraphs are uploaded.

aj: thanks — if we need a quick rollback policy for dedicated customers, let's draft a one-liner fallback note for release notes.

maria: noted. drafting fallback PR after artifacts. :thumbsup:
